context.title: Moab's Pride Humbled
context.summary: A long lament over Moab names town after town as its god Chemosh goes into exile and complacent Moab is poured out like wine left on its dregs. The prophet mourns with Moab, and the chapter ends with a promise of restoration.
context.background: Moab, east of the Dead Sea, worshiped Chemosh (1 Kings 11:7); King Mesha's inscription, the Mesha Stele, credits Chemosh with Moab's victories over Israel in the 800s BC. Much of this chapter echoes Isaiah 15–16, and vv. 45–46 echo an old victory song in Numbers 21:28-29. The historian Josephus says Nebuchadnezzar subdued Moab and Ammon in 582 BC.

customs.note: Wine was poured from jar to jar to separate it from its sediment. Left undisturbed, it kept a harsh taste. Moab, never exiled, has grown complacent.

watchFor: The prophet's heart sounds 'like pipes' for Moab (v. 36).
Hope at the end: 'Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab' (v. 47).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Chemosh
people.summary: The destroyer, subduer, or fish-god, the god of the Moabites (Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:7, 13, 46). The worship of this god, “the abomination of Moab,” was introduced at Jerusalem by Solomon (1 Kings 11:7), but was abolished by Josiah (2 Kings 23:13).

people.name: Sihon
people.summary: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them.

places.name: Kiriathaim
places.summary: A town on the east of Jordan (Gen. 14:5; Deut. 2:9, 10). It was assigned to the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37). In the time of Ezekiel (25:9) it was one of the four cities which formed the “glory of Moab” (comp. Jer. 48:1, 23).

places.name: Misgab
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1274 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Nebo
places.summary: A Chaldean god whose worship was introduced into Assyria by Pul (Isa. 46:1; Jer. 48:1). To this idol was dedicated the great temple whose ruins are still seen at Birs Nimrud.

places.name: Heshbon
places.summary: Intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Josh. 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Num. 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Josh. 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37).

places.name: Madmen
places.summary: Ibid., a Moabite town threatened with the sword of the Babylonians (Jer. 48:2).

places.name: Horonaim
places.summary: Two caverns, a city of Moab to the south of the Arnon, built, apparently, upon an eminence, and a place of some importance (Isa. 15:5; Jer. 48:3, 5, 34).

places.name: Luhith
places.summary: Made of boards, a Moabitish place between Zoar and Horonaim (Isa. 15:5; Jer. 48:5).

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Dibon
places.summary: A city in Moab (Num. 21:30); called also Dibon-gad (33:45), because it was built by Gad and Dimon (Isa. 15:9).

places.name: Aroer
places.summary: A town on the north bank of the Arnon (Deut. 4:48; Judg. 11:26; 2 Kings 10:33), the southern boundary of the kingdom of Sihon (Josh. 12:2).

places.name: Arnon
places.summary: Swift, the southern boundary of the territory of Israel beyond Jordan, separating it from the land of Moab (Deut. 3:8, 16). This river (referred to twenty-four times in the Bible) rises in the mountains of Gilead, and after a circuitous course of about 80 miles through a deep ravine it falls into the Dead Sea nearly opposite Engedi.

places.name: Mephaath
places.summary: Splendour, a Levitical city (Josh. 21:37) of the tribe of Reuben (13:18).

places.name: Beth-diblathaim
places.summary: House of two cakes of figs, a city of Moab, upon which Jeremiah (48:22) denounced destruction. It is called also Almon-diblathaim (Num. 33:46) and Diblath (Ezek. 6:14).

places.name: Beth-gamul
places.summary: Camel-house, a city in the “plain country” of Moab denounced by the prophet (Jer. 48:23); probably the modern Um-el-Jemal, near Bozrah, one of the deserted cities of the Hauran.

places.name: Bozrah
places.summary: A Moabite city in the “plain country” (Jer. 48:24), i.e., on the high level down on the east of the Dead Sea.

places.name: Kerioth
places.summary: A city of Moab (Jer. 48:24, 41), called Kirioth (Amos 2:2).

places.name: Jazer
places.summary: He (God) helps, a city of the Amorites on the east of Jordan, and assigned, with neighbouring places in Gilead, to Gad (Num. 32:1, 35; Josh. 13:25).

places.name: sea of Jazer
places.summary: water

places.name: Sibmah
places.summary: Coolness; fragrance, a town in Reuben, in the territory of Moab, on the east of Jordan (Josh. 13:19); called also Shebam and Shibmah (Num. 32:3, 38).

places.name: Eglath-shelishiyah
places.summary: Heb. ‘eglah, (Deut. 21:4, 6; Jer. 46:20).

places.name: Elealeh
places.summary: God has ascended, a place in the pastoral country east of Jordan, in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:3, 37). It is not again mentioned till the time of Isaiah (15:4; 16:9) and Jeremiah (48:34).

places.name: Jahaz
places.summary: Trodden down (called also Jahaza, Josh. 13:18; Jahazah, 21:36; Jahzah, 1 Chr. 6:78), a town where Sihon was defeated, in the borders of Moab and in the land of the Ammonites beyond Jordan, and north of the river Arnon (Num. 21:23; Deut. 2:32).

places.name: Nimrim
places.summary: The stream of the leopards, a stream in Moab (Isa. 15:6; Jer. 48:34); probably the modern Wady en-Nemeirah, a rich, verdant spot at the south-eastern end of the Dead Sea.

places.name: Zoar
places.summary: Small, a town on the east or south-east of the Dead Sea, to which Lot and his daughters fled from Sodom (Gen. 19:22, 23). It was originally called Bela (14:2, 8).

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
